disposition_mapping.rationale: Due-item selection is automated and combined with proposal generation in a single ERP-driven step, but still consumes approved matched invoices and payment terms as required (PRE-R-01).

Payment proposal generation survives as the second half of the automated TS-01 step, satisfying the step-preservation requirement (PRE-R-08) while eliminating a redundant manual hand-off between selection and grouping.

Proposal review survives (PRE-R-09) but is restructured around an automated exception-screening engine that pre-flags duplicates, blocked vendors and bank-detail changes, letting the supervisor focus human judgment on true exceptions. It remains before approval and before file release, preserving PRE-R-02 and PRE-R-03.

Payment approval survives unchanged as a distinct human decision by an authorised signatory (PRE-R-10), remaining after review (PRE-R-02) and before file release (PRE-R-05), and performed by an actor distinct from the automated proposal-generation step (PRE-R-04).
Payment file generation and release to bank survives as a discrete treasury-owned step (PRE-R-11), occurring after proposal review and approval.

Bank confirmation receipt is unconstrained by design and is absorbed into the automated bank-matching capability within TS-05, eliminating a separate manual reconciliation hand-off while preserving the confirmation output used downstream.

Posting and clearing survives but is restructured to be automation-driven, continuing to consume the bank settlement confirmation (PRE-R-06) and the settlement-date exchange rate (PRE-R-07) so FX differences remain recognised per IAS 21 (KB-07, KB-08) and subledger/GL evidence remains traceable per IAS 1 (KB-02) and IFRS 9 recognition/derecognition timing (KB-11).

Remittance advice is unconstrained by design and is absorbed into an automated notification step triggered directly from settlement confirmation, removing manual effort while preserving vendor communication of settled invoices.

steps.actor: ERP system (automated), with AP analyst oversight
steps.description: The ERP automatically identifies approved, matched invoices (including foreign-currency items) falling due under their payment terms and generates a payment proposal grouped by vendor, currency and payment method. An AP analyst provides oversight and can intervene on flagged items, but selection and grouping logic run as a scheduled automated job rather than a manual pull.
steps.name: Automated due-item selection and payment proposal generation

steps.actor: AP supervisor, with automated exception-screening engine
steps.description: An automated screening engine checks the proposal against the vendor bank-detail change log and payment history to flag duplicate payments, blocked vendors, and recently changed bank details. The AP supervisor reviews the flagged exceptions specifically (rather than re-checking every line manually), confirms dispositions, and removes or holds exception items before the proposal proceeds.
steps.name: Automated exception screening and proposal review

steps.description: The reviewed proposal is approved for payment by an authorised signatory within delegated limits. This decision remains a distinct human judgment separate from both proposal generation and proposal review.
steps.name: Payment approval

steps.description: The approved proposal is converted into a bank payment file and released to the bank, with dual-control release confirmation retained for high-value or flagged batches.
steps.name: Payment file generation and release to bank

steps.actor: GL accountant, with automated bank reconciliation and posting engine
steps.description: An automated bank reconciliation engine ingests the bank statement/confirmation feed, matches executed payments to the transmitted file, and triggers posting of settled payments: clearing open items in the AP subledger and recording cash in the GL, applying the settlement-date exchange rate and recognising foreign-currency settlement differences. The GL accountant reviews system-generated postings and handles unmatched or exception items.
steps.name: Automated bank settlement matching, posting and clearing

steps.description: Upon confirmed settlement, the ERP automatically generates and transmits remittance advice to each vendor detailing the invoices settled by each payment, without manual intervention.
steps.name: Automated remittance advice to vendors
